 Judgment:

1. The present is a complaint filed under section 26/59 of the FSS Act, 2006 alleging that the accused persons namely Vishwa Prakash and DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another Rishabh Mehta violated the provisions of the FSS Act and Rules.

entities.text: DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another Rishabh Mehta
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accused no. 1 Vishwa Prakash son of Late Sh. Budh Prakash, being FBO/Proprietor of M/s. S.K Sweets at Shop no. 10,11 & 12 Sanwal Nagar, Sadiq Nagar, New Delhi-110049 from where the food article, that is, 'Boondi Laddoo' was lifted for sampling.

2. As per the complaint, on 01.11.2013, the food officials consisting of FSO Ranjeet Singh and FA Siya Ram under the supervision of DO Shyam Lal reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. S.K Sweets at Shop no. 10,11 & 12 Sanwal Nagar, Sadiq Nagar, New Delhi-110049, where the accused no. 1 Vishwa Prakash was found conducting the business of various food articles, which Da/Fso vs Vishwa Prakash And Another on 28 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137579736/
1 were lying stored for sale for human consumption.

entities.text: Da/Fso vs Vishwa Prakash And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The FSO disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Boondi Laddoo from the vendor lying in an open tray bearing no label declaration, to which he agreed.
The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the FSS Act and Rules.

The sample was divided into four counterparts by putting 500 grams of Boondi Ladoo into each of the clean and dry plastic jars making it as one counterpart of the sample and adding 40 drops of formalin into each sample jar with the help of clean and dry dropper and gently shaken for proper dispersion of preservative.

Each sample was separately packed, fastened,
marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the Notice as per Form-VA, Panchnama, etc.
The price of sample was paid to the FBO/accused no. 1 Vishwa Prakash.
All the documents were read over and explained to FBO/accused no. 1 Vishwa Prakash and he signed the same in Hindi after understanding the same.

FBO/accused no. 1 Vishwa Prakash did DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another not make any request to send one counterpart to Accredited laboratory for testing under Section 47 (1) (c)(iii) and Notice was also sent to the suppliers/manufacturer of the sampled articles of food Boondi Ladoo.

entities.text: DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Food Analyst in intact condition and the other three counterparts were deposited with DO as at the time of sampling FBO/

accused no. 1 Vishwa Prakash did not make any request to the Food Safety Officer to send one counterpart sample to Accredited Laboratory for testing under section 47 (1)(c)(iii) of FSS Act, 2006 r/w Rule 2.4.5 of FSS Rules, 2011.

3. The Food Analyst vide its report dated 13.11.2013 opined that the sample was unsafe because the total dye content of the synthetic colour used, which exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 100ppm.

The DO, Sh. Shyam Lal sent the report of the Food Analyst to the Food Business Operator/
accused no. 1 Vishwa Prakash for giving him an opportunity to file an appeal against the Food Analyst U/s. 46 (4) of FSS Act, 2006 for sending one part of the sample to Referral Food Laboratory if so desired and the FBO/accused preferred an appeal against the report of Food Analyst and hence one counterpart of the aforesaid sample was sent to RFL, Mysore vide Report dated 29.01.2014,
Director, RFL, Mysore opined that "the sample was unsafe as defined u/s 3(1)(zz)(viii) of FSS Act,
2006 as it did not conform to the standards as laid down for Food Article under FSS Act, 2006 and Rules 2011 as the added artificial colouring matter exceeded the maximum permissible limit of 100 ppm.

4. It was further revealed during investigation that the FBO/accused DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another no. 1 Vishwa Prakash was the FBO-cum-proprietor of M/s. S.K Sweets at Shop no. 10,11 & 12 Sanwal Nagar, Sadiq Nagar, New Delhi-49 at the time of taking the sample and looks after day to day business and such he was in charge and responsible for the day to day business and the sampled food article of 'Boondi Laddoo' was manufactured by the FBO himself.

sentences.text: 5. After completion of investigation, consent under section 42(4) of the FSS Act was obtained from the Director, PFA.

The complaint was then filed in the court alleging violation of section 26(2)(i) of FSS Act, 2006 r/w Section 3(1) (zz)(viii) of FSS Act, 2006 and also for violation of Regulation No.
3.1.2(7) of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products standards and Food Additives) Regulations,
2011 r/w Regulation No. 3.1.2(6) of FSS ( Food Products Standards and Food Additives)

The accused persons were summoned.

On the basis of report of Director, RFL, prima facie notice for the violation of Section 26(2)(i) r/w section 3(1) (zz)(viii) of FSS Act, 2006 and Regulation No. 3.1.2.6(ii) and 3.1.2.7 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations,
2011, punishable u/s. 59 (i) of FSS Act, 2006, were framed against the accused persons to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

sentences.text: DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another 7.
At the trial, prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case.

PW-1 FSO Ranjeet Singh,
PW-2 DO Shyam Lal, PW3 FA Siya Ram were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings.

All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 01.11.2013 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 2 kg Boondi Laddoo lying in an open carton rack bearing no label declaration, breaking it into smallest possible pieces, mixing/ homogenizing it, dividing it in four parts and putting in clean and dry bottles,
adding 40 drops of formalin in each bottle as preservative, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of FBO/accused and witnesses.
They also proved the necessary documents including the FBO receipt Ex. PW-1/A, Notice Ex. PW-1/B.
The accused/FBO disclosed that he had purchased the sample commodity from M Laddoo Wala, F-3, Jeewan Park, Pankha Road, New Delhi vide bill No. 469 dated 28.10.2013.
The copy of bill/cash memo of M. Laddoo Wala was Ex.PW1/B1.
Notice under Rule 2.4.1(4) of Form VA was Ex.PW1/B2.

Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C.
Raid Report Ex. PW-1/D.

On the next working day, one counterpart sample deposited with Food Analyst vide receipt Ex.PW-1/E and the four counterpart deposited with DO is Ex.PW-1/F as accused/FBO Vishwa Prakash did not request to send another counterpart sample for analysis.
Food Analyst report Ex. PW-1/G wherein it was stated that the sample was unsafe, was received and investigation was started.

Letter sent by DO giving accused/FBO opportunity to file appeal u/s.
46(4) of FSS Act is Ex.PW1/H and request letter of accused is Ex.PW1/1-I.
The result of RFL is DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another Ex.PW1/J.

entities.text: DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Letter sent to FBO Vishwa Prakash and one reminder were Ex.PW1/K and Ex.PW1/K1.
Reply from FBO is Ex.PW1/K2.

Letters sent to M.
Laddoo Wala/supplier
and one reminder were Ex.PW1/L and Ex.PW1/L1 and he did not receive any reply.
Letter sent to VATO Ward No. 61 and 96 and one reminder for constitution of M. Laddoo Wala and S.K. Sweets were Ex.PW1/M, Ex.PW1/M1 and Ex.PW1/M2.

The replies from AC Ward No.
61 were Ex.PW1/M3 and Ex.PW1/M4.
8.
After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW-1/O was taken from the Commissioner, Food Safety and the complaint Ex. PW-1/P was filed in the court.
These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel wherein PW1 stated during his cross- examination that he had lifted the sample using a clean and dry spoon.

He also stated that on the basis of investigation,
he was satisfied that the commodity had been sold to accused No. 2 by accused No. 1.

During his cross-examination by Ld. Counsel for Accused No. 2, he stated it might have been possible that Ex.PW1/L sent to accused No.2 had returned undelivered and the original letter was given to him which he placed on record.

He had further stated that he had also sent a reminder through the Da/Fso vs Vishwa Prakash And Another on 28 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137579736/
3 dispatch section.

entities.text: Da/Fso vs Vishwa Prakash And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He admitted that no mode of service could be seen on the document.
He admitted that letter Ex.PW1/L2 dated 28.11.2013 was received by him and further admitted that no written communication was done with accused No. 2 after receipt of their reply.

He further stated that the basis of his being satisfied that the product had been supplied by accused No. 2 to accused No. 1 is that on the day of sampling, accused No. 1 had telephonically called the accused No. 2 who also spoke to him and DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another accused No. 2 had accepted that the product had been supplied by them.

PW3 stated during his cross-examination by Ld. Counsel for accused No. 2 that he could not say whether the copy of bill Ex.PW1/B1 were sent by FBO alongwith his letter dated 29.05.2014 Ex.PW1/K2.
9.

Statement of the accused persons under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 16.01.2019 wherein Accused No. 1 admitted the sample proceedings but added that sample commodity was purchased by him from M. Laddoo Wala vide bill No. 469 dated 28.10.2013 and the sample was given of the sample laddoo which were purchased from M. Laddoo Wala.
He added also that he had made no adulteration.
Accused No. 2 Rishabh Mehta stated in his examination U/s. 313 CrPC that he did not know anything about the sample proceedings as he was not present at the spot.

He further stated that as had not supplied the said Boondi Laddoos to accused Vishwa Prakash and the bill was not issued from their firm as the same does not bear any TIN number of their firm or signature of any of the person of the issuance of the said bill.

He also stated that accused No. 1 had given his name with malafide intention to avoid payment of old bills as he had already mentioned in his reply dated 28.11.2013 Ex.PW1/L2.
10.

Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt, on the ground that the accused persons have not been able to rebut the findings of the Director, RFL report.
It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony.
DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another 11.
On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel for accused No. 1 has submitted that the sampled commodity was supplied by accused No. 2 and they have placed on record to prove the same.
On the other hand, Ld. Defence counsel for accused No. 2 has argued that he did receive the letter Ex.PW1/L.
He further argued that the accused No. 2 ws not the manufacturer of the Boondi Ke Laddoo and the sample commodity did not belong to him.
12. I have heard the arguments advanced by Ld. SPP for the complainant and Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused and have carefully perused the material available on record.

13. It is to be understood that the notice framed against the accused persons are for violation of Section 26(2)(i) r/w section 3(1) (zz)(viii) of FSS Act, 2006 and Regulation No. 3.1.2.6(ii) and 3.1.2.7 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011,
punishable u/s. 59 (i) of FSS Act, 2006 which are as under :
Da/Fso vs Vishwa Prakash And Another on 28 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137579736/
4 Section 26(2)(i) of FSS Act deals with Responsibilities of the food business operator - (1) Every food business operator shall ensure that the article of food satisfy the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder at all stages of production, processing, import, distribution and sale within the business under his control.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
(2) No food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacture, store, sell or distribute any article of food- (i) which is unsafe; or.....
DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another Section 3 (1) (zz) (viii) deals with "unsafe food" means an article of food whose nature, substance or qualit y is so affected as to render it injuriously to health................. by the presence of any colouring matter or preservatives other than that specified in respect thereof; or Section 26 (2) (i) of FSS Act provides that - no food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf shall manufacture, store, sell or distribute any article of food- which is unsafe.......

entities.text: DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another Section 3 (1) (zz) (viii)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Regulation No. 3.1.2 (6) and (7) of FSS (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation 2011 deals with use of permitted synthetic food colours and prescribes their limit of synthetic food colour which have been prohibited.

entities.text: FSS (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Section 59 (i) of FSS Act deals with Punishment for unsafe food - it states that any person who, whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf, manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports and article of food for human consumption which is unsafe shall be punishable - where such failure or contravention does not result in injury, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and also with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.

14. The incriminating material on the basis of which the sample of Boondi Laddoo has been failed by the Food Analyst as well as by the Director, RFL, is that as per both the reports, the sample was unsafe as synthetic food colouring matter was found in the sampled food DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another article exceeding the maximum prescribed standards of 100ppm.
15.

Both the report of the Director, RFL, and the report of the Food Analyst clearly mention that the synthetic colouring matter present in the sampled food article exceeded the maximum prescribed limit of 100 ppm.

The defence has not been able to rebut or bring any evidence on record to show that the spoon or the bottles in which the sampled food article was collected, were not clean and dry,
as has been the suggestions made by them during the cross-examination of the witnesses.

Further,
merely stating so during the cross-examination of witnesses without adducing evidence on record to corroborate the said suggestions is not enough to rebut the evidence laid forth by the complainant,
which per se is admissible as per law.
16.
The copy of the bill Ex.PW1/B-1 which was issued by the M. Laddoo Wala to the proprietorship concern of M/s. S.K. Sweets dated 28.10.2013.
The sample proceedings are of 01.11.2013.

In fact,
even Ex.PW1/B which is notice in Form VA at point X to X, it has been mentioned by accused No. 1 in his own handwriting that he had purchased the sampled food article from M. Laddoo Wala Da/Fso vs Vishwa Prakash And Another on 28 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137579736/
5

entities.text: M. Laddoo Wala Da/Fso vs Vishwa Prakash And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: against bill No. 469 on 28.10.2013.

Even PW1 has stated during his cross- examination that he was satisfied on the basis of investigation conducted that the product had been supplied by accused No.
2.
PW1 even explained the basis of his satisfaction during cross-examination.
17. In fact, the original bill has been placed on record by accused No. 1.
Accordingly, accused No. 1 Vishwa Prakash is hereby acquitted in the present case.
DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another 18.
Qua accused No. 2 Rishabh Mehta, it is seen that he has denied by letter dated 28.11.2013 that they had supplied the proprietorship concern of M/s. S.K. Sweets any laddoos.
However, as already discussed, the original bill is already on record.

No document or proof has been lead on behalf of accused No. 2 to show that they had not issued any such bill or that the sampled food article Boondi ke Laddoo was not manufactured and supplied by them to M/s. S.K. Sweets.
They have not produced any bill book or any other document to corroborate their arguments that the series of bill No. 400 to 500 wee not in use on 28.10.2013.

Further, the address of the M/s. M. Laddoo Wala as per the bill Ex.PW1/B is correct and same to that of accused No. 2 as per record and merely because the TIN number has not been provided in the receipts cannot be the sole criteria to reject the bill,
when the accused No. 2 Rishabh Mehta has not lead any evidence or any corroborative proof or even produced any other bill to show as to what were the bills that were generally issued by M/s. M.
Laddoo Wala.
19. Another defence taken by Ld. Counsel for accused No. 2 that Ex.PW1/L1 was not served upon the accused No. 2.
Ex.PW1/L is the letter dated 05.03.2014 issued by Food Officials regarding information from M. Laddoo Wala.
Another letter which is the reminder dated 26.05.2014 was also sent which is Ex.PW1/L1.
The entry No. 1245 is also seen to have been made on the aforesaid letter and the same is seen to be an office copy.
Accused No. 2 was aware of the sample proceedings and was sent the official communication by the concerned Food Officials.
The official members are also present on all communications so sent to accused persons in the present case.
DA/FSO Vs Vishwa Prakash and another
Even though as already discussed, the accused No. 2 has denied supplying the sampled food article to accused No. 1.
The entire evidence lead during trial proves that the sampled commodity was manufactured and supplied by accused No. 1.
Even the Food Safety Officer, Mr. Ranjeet Singh has shown his satisfaction to the aforesaid fact and has admitted talking telephonically to accused No. 2.
Furthermore, no proof has also been lead on behalf of accused No. 2 to show that accused No. 1 had outstanding balance against him as has been his defence.

20. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid facts and discussions, there is sufficient evidence on record too show that accused No. 2 Rishabh Mehta was the manufacturer and supplier of the sampled food article "Boondi Laddoo" which was found unsafe due to presence of synthetic colours beyond the permissible limit.

Accused No. 2 Rishabh Mehta is accordingly convicted for the violation of Section 26(2)(i) of FSS Act r/w section 3(1) (zz)(viii) of FSS Act and Regulation No. 3.1.2.6(ii) and 3.1.2.7 of Da/Fso vs Vishwa Prakash And Another on 28 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137579736/
6 FSS Act (Food Product Standard and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, punishable u/s. 59 (i) of FSS Act.
21.
